newsitem.title: UK: Major sees BoE overdeflating British economy.
newsitem.headline: Major sees BoE overdeflating British economy.

text.p: Leader of the opposition Conservative Party John Major on Wednesday predicted that the Bank of England would use its new powers to regulate British interest rates to "overdeflate" the economy.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced last week that he was giving the new powers to the Bank in order to control inflation at rates to be determined by the Government.
In a parliamentary speech responding to the government's legislative programme announced earlier, Major, prime minister until the May 1 election, said he believed the idea would "work only too well".
"The Bank will meet its remit; of that I think we can be reasonably confident," Major, who is also a former Chancellor of the Exchequer, said.
"And to do it it will if anything overperform. It will overdeflate the economy to make sure that it meets the particular remit that the Chancellor has given it," he added.
"As a result of that, unemployment will be higher than it would be, and growth will be lower than it otherwise would be." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
